analysis.investment_thesis: EPL passes the minimum Magic Formula bar with a ROCE of ~17.5% and an earnings yield of ~10.3% (EBIT ₹837 Cr / EV ~₹8,090 Cr), but neither metric clears my attractiveness thresholds of 12% earnings yield and 25%+ ROIC. At current pricing, this is a decent business trading at a fair — not bargain — valuation.
key_strengths: Improving EBIT trajectory: Operating Income surged from ₹569 Cr (2022) to ₹837 Cr (2025), signaling recovering operational leverage
Strong OCF generation: ₹795 Cr OCF in FY25 with FCF of ₹439 Cr — 5/5 years of positive operating cash flow
Manageable leverage: D/E of 0.32 with Total Debt ₹802 Cr vs Total Equity ₹2,624 Cr keeps balance sheet stable
key_risks: Finance costs nearly tripled: from ₹43 Cr (2021) to ₹114 Cr (2025), compressing net earnings despite EBIT growth
Capital-intensive model: Capex of ₹363 Cr in FY25 (~43% of OCF) limits FCF conversion — Greenblatt prefers asset-light businesses with high FCF yield
Low promoter holding of 26.38% signals limited insider conviction; revenue CAGR of only 7.9% over 9 years limits Magic Formula ranking upside
red_flags: Earnings Yield of ~10.3% falls below the 12% Magic Formula attractiveness threshold — not cheap enough to qualify as a bargain
EBITDA CAGR of 5.8% (9Y) is below revenue growth of 7.9% — margin erosion at the EBITDA level over the long arc
Finance cost explosion (43→114 Cr in 4 years) suggests debt-funded capex cycle that has yet to fully earn back its cost of capital
analysis.detailed_analysis:
Running the Magic Formula: Enterprise Value = Market Cap ₹7,479 Cr + Net Debt (₹802 Cr - ₹191 Cr cash) = ~₹8,090 Cr. EBIT (Operating Income FY25) = ₹837 Cr. Earnings Yield = 837/8,090 = **10.3%** — below my 12% threshold for "attractive." On the return side, stated ROCE of 17.5% is respectable but falls short of the 25%+ I look for in truly excellent businesses. A packaging company competing globally on laminated tubes is inherently capital-heavy, which structurally limits how high ROIC can climb. The Magic Formula rewards capital-light compounders; EPL is not that.

The business trajectory is actually improving — FY25 net profit of ₹364 Cr is the best in the series, OCF hit ₹795 Cr, and operating margins expanded from a 2022 trough. But these improvements are partly offset by surging finance costs (₹114 Cr vs ₹40 Cr in 2022) from an aggressive capex cycle, and revenue growth of ~8% CAGR over 9 years is uninspiring. EPL screens as a "pass" on quality and a "marginal miss" on value — exactly the middle-of-the-road outcome the Magic Formula systematically avoids in favor of companies that rank in the top decile on both dimensions simultaneously.
